title: Conditional surge slicing and autorecover rollout controller for LTS-safe upgrades
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our current staged rollout primitives (simple percent ramps + static canaries) do not adequately protect LTS customers during high-variance traffic surges or multi-tenant bursts. We saw a recent incident where a mid-ramp change caused tail latency spikes for a small set of enterprise routes; static ramps did not react quickly enough and manual rollback was required.

Proposal: Implement a rollout controller that combines two complementary mechanisms: 1) conditional surge-slicing — dynamic cohort partitioning that isolates customers/routes into smaller 'slices' during abnormal telemetry events; and 2) autorecover policies — automated temporary fallback actions (traffic carve-outs, immediate rollback to pinned LTS variant, or live model degrading) when safety thresholds are exceeded. The controller should: 1) use short-window anomaly detectors (p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, memory pressure) with Bayesian early-stop rules; 2) operate at route and token-space granularity so high-risk routes can be carved out without blocking global ramp; 3) integrate with feature flags to allow per-customer opt-outs and emergency hold; 4) surface signals in Console for human-in-the-loop overrides and post-mortem traces.

Design considerations and trade-offs:
- Aggressiveness vs noise: aggressive early-stop reduces blast radius but increases false positives. We will tune using synthetic surge tests and a staged enablement on non-LTS traffic.
- Isolation cost: creating fine-grained slices increases routing complexity and slightly higher control-plane overhead. We limit slice cardinality by combining heuristics (high-traffic routes + enterprise customer IDs).
- Fallback fidelity: fallback to LTS-pinned model preserves correctness but may increase cost. We prefer temporary carve-outs to full rollback when feasible.

Success criteria: automatic detection and mitigation for >90% of injected surge experiments in canary lab, <1% false positive intervention on production baseline, no measurable increase in median latency for unaffected routes.

Rollout plan: prototype -> internal canary -> non-LTS canary -> gradual LTS opt-in (customer-first opt-in) -> full LTS enablement with audit logging and runbook.

See attached design doc and runbook links for sequence diagrams, policy DSL, and metrics queries.

2026-02-20 - Design review: PMs (Lina Park) requested explicit per-tenant opt-out and audit trail for GDPR customers. Security said feature flags must be SSO-restricted for emergency overrides. See notes in design doc.

2026-02-25 - Engineering update: Prototype for slice router complete. Local E2E harness shows carve-out latency drop for simulated burst. Perf regression <2% median on control routes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4123

2026-03-01 - QA: Ran 50 synthetic surge experiments in staging. Autorecover triggered in 46/50 and correctly carved traffic to fallback pool. False-positive rate observed: 4%. Test plan updated to include longer tail scenarios and chaos injection. Test run artifacts: https://internal.ci/redwood/builds/6123
2026-03-03 - Security review: No secrets exposure. KMS/HSM integration not required for controller configuration. Security review complete (ticket SEC-2026-45).
2026-03-05 - Pending: Add Console UI for slice visualization and manual hold. Blocker: telemetry cardinality API improvements (ENG-42109) needed before non-LTS ramp.
